The purpose of this section is to describe what is expected

Companion Animal Travel Desk Service Standards

The Companion Animal Travel Desk supports travelers who are flying with animals and helps make each handoff calm, clear, and humane. Staff should listen closely, give plain guidance, and keep the traveler informed about what happens next. When a pet arrives at the desk, confirm the booking details, check the travel documents that are presented, and make sure the animal is ready for the next step without causing stress.

Handlers must use gentle language and steady movements around animals, and they should avoid crowding, sudden noise, or any action that might unsettle the pet. If a traveler seems worried, offer practical help first and keep the explanation simple. Staff should also watch for signs that an animal needs extra care and bring in the senior coordinator when the situation calls for it. <<FACT F120>> If a traveler reports a problem with an animal in transit, the desk should record the details carefully, preserve the supporting paperwork, and guide the traveler toward the proper follow-up channel without delay.

The desk should work in a way that keeps the traveler respected and the animal safe. Do not promise an outcome you cannot confirm, do not guess at policy, and do not send a traveler away with unanswered concerns if you can help them move forward. When boarding support is needed, coordinate with the welcome team and the gate staff so the handoff stays smooth and calm. If a request does not fit the usual process, explain the next step in direct words and stay with the traveler until they understand what will happen.

For questions about exceptions, travel concerns, or incident reporting, contact the senior coordinator or the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
